sentences.text:
By this pre-arrest bail application filed under Section 438 of the CrPC, the five petitioners, namely,
1.Md. Mannas Ali, 2. Mozibur Rahman, 3. Dildar Hussain, 4. Hakimul Islam and 5. Amradul Islam have sought for releasing them on bail in connection with the Moirabari P.S. Case No.423/2020,
registered under Sections 269/272/426/420/34 of the IPC.

Heard Mr. A. Ganguly, learned counsel for the petitioners as well as Mr. R.J. Baruah, learned Addl.
P.P., Assam for the State respondent and perused the record and the case diary produced.
On the allegation that the present petitioners are running a jiggery factory, wherein they were manufacturing adulterated jiggery and thereby cheated the public, the FIR was lodged by the ASI of Police of Moirabari P.S. and accordingly the Moirabari P.S. Case No.423/2020 was registered.
The case diary reveals that the I.O. has sent the sample of the jiggery for forensic examination and the collected sample is found to be adulterated.

This Court while dealing with such matter in Criminal Petition No.487/2016, vide judgment and order Page No.# 3/3 dated 28.05.2019 had elaborately dealt with such matter and opined that in Page No.# 1/3 vs The State Of Assam on 10 December, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70933914/
2 view of the Special Act that has been enacted to examine food items under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short 'the FSS Act'), registration of FIR on such matter of adulteration is bad in law.
With the same assertion, it can be held that registration of the FIR by the I.O., without intimating the appropriate authority is not proper.
The I.O. is accordingly directed to proceed with the proper procedure, as indicated in the aforesaid judgment in Criminal Petition No.487/2016.
However considering all entirety, the interim bail so granted earlier, is hereby made absolute.
Return back the case diary forthwith.
